justification: Backend, additive, fail-safe: when our ingested spatial coverage is missing riparian/wetlands/biodiversity for an LGA, the brief now live point-queries the NSW Planning/Protection layer for THIS lot and reports the real fact (present / none here) instead of leaking an internal 'Layer not ingested for this LGA' gap. DB coverage still wins; a failed live query or missing coords falls back to the existing NOT_AVAILABLE state. No regulatory values are hardcoded; the value is a boolean presence flag from the authoritative government layer.

pre_impl.existing_data: _build_environmental (intelligence_brief.py) set riparian/wetlands/biodiversity to NOT_AVAILABLE + reason 'Layer not ingested for this LGA' whenever the layer was absent from overlays_data.covered_layers — collapsing 'not loaded', 'not relevant', and 'genuinely clear' into one string. portal_constraints already point-queries the same Planning/Protection service (fetch_anef=layer 2, drinking_water=layer 3) via query_arcgis_point.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The brief assumed a missing layer means 'no data', when for these live-queryable layers the truth (present at this lot vs none here) is obtainable per-lot regardless of our ingestion. Verified live: 25 Empire St returns present=False for riparian/wetlands/biodiversity (a real 'none here', not a gap).
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Reuses query_arcgis_point (no new query infra). One new fail-safe fetcher fetch_protection_overlay(lat,lng,layer_id) and one helper _overlay_field inside _build_environmental. lat/lng are threaded into _build_environmental at both existing call sites. The fetcher is only called when the layer is NOT in covered_layers.
pre_impl.external_source_error: fetch_protection_overlay wraps query_arcgis_point in try/except and returns None on any failure; _overlay_field returns None on a missing import or exception. Either way the field falls back to the prior NOT_AVAILABLE 'Layer not ingested' state, so a slow or down government API never blocks the brief and never over-states presence.
pre_impl.frontend_type: Backend only. The DataField value stays a boolean (present True / none False) so the EnvironmentalConstraints pydantic schema is unchanged; only the source string ('live_protection_overlay') and the confidence (AUTHORITATIVE instead of NOT_AVAILABLE) change when the live query succeeds.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: an un-ingested layer showed internal jargon 'Layer not ingested for this LGA'. After: the user sees the real per-lot fact (riparian/wetland present: yes/no) for live-queryable layers, and only sees the honest 'not assessed' fallback when both our DB and the live query have nothing.

functions.name: fetch_protection_overlay
functions.input: the latitude, longitude and a Planning/Protection layer id (riparian 7, wetlands 11, biodiversity 10) for one property
functions.output: a dict with present True plus the layer class, present False for a queried-but-empty lot, or None when the query fails
functions.if_none: any request exception returns None so the caller keeps the conservative not-assessed fallback rather than asserting absence

functions.name: _overlay_field
functions.input: the layer key, the ingested DB presence flag and the Protection layer id for one overlay field
functions.output: a DataField using DB coverage first, else the live per-lot fact, else the conservative NOT_AVAILABLE not-ingested fallback
functions.if_none: with no DB coverage, no coordinates and no live result it returns the existing NOT_AVAILABLE field unchanged from before

values: N/A - no regulatory values are hardcoded. The value is a boolean presence flag read from the authoritative NSW Planning/Protection layer; layer ids (7/11/10) mirror the existing ingest config, not invented planning numbers.
queries: N/A - no database query. The change adds a live ArcGIS point query that reuses the already-reviewed query_arcgis_point helper against the same Protection service other fetchers use.

break_it.scenario: The live Protection query times out or errors while assembling the brief
break_it.what_happens: a naive live call could crash the environmental section or invent a presence value the lot does not have
break_it.how: fetch_protection_overlay returns None on any exception and _overlay_field then keeps the conservative NOT_AVAILABLE 'not ingested' field

break_it.scenario: The property has no resolved coordinates so a live query is impossible
break_it.what_happens: calling the live layer with None coordinates would error or query the wrong place
break_it.how: the live branch runs only when lat and lng are both present; otherwise it returns the existing NOT_AVAILABLE fallback with no call

break_it.scenario: Our database already covers the layer for this LGA
break_it.what_happens: an unnecessary live call would add latency and could disagree with the ingested value
break_it.how: _overlay_field returns the DB-backed DataField first and never calls the live fetcher when the layer is in covered_layers

break_it.scenario: The live query runs and the lot genuinely has nothing in the layer
break_it.what_happens: showing 'not assessed' would hide that we actually checked and the lot is clear
break_it.repro: pytest tests/test_overlay_live_fallback.py::test_live_absent_is_a_clean_false ; live 25 Empire St returns present False for all three
break_it.how: a successful empty query returns present False which becomes a boolean False (a real 'none here'), confidence AUTHORITATIVE, not NOT_AVAILABLE

post_merge.manual_verify: Run a live brief in an un-ingested LGA (e.g. Inner West 25 Empire St) — riparian/wetlands/biodiversity should show a real Yes/No from the live Protection query, not 'Layer not ingested'. Confirm an ingested LGA still uses the DB value and makes no extra live call. The same helper can later extend to other live-queryable Protection layers; per-layer staleness metadata (distinguishing 'checked, none' from 'never loaded') for non-live layers remains a follow-up.
